newsitem.title: USA: Former U.S. presidents say Reagan debilitated. [CORRECTED 18:59 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. presidents say Reagan debilitated. [CORRECTED 18:59 GMT]

text.p: Former U.S. President Ronald Reagan's physical appearance is good, but Alzheimer's disease has left him unable to handle public appearances, his presidential colleagues said on Thursday (corrects from Wednesday).
Reagan was the only living former U.S. president not to attend a rededication ceremony for the Gerald R. Ford Museum, which is opening new exhibits here.

"I saw him a couple of months ago and this disease is such that it would be impossible for him to be at a meeting like this and respond to your questions," former President George Bush told a news conference on Thursday that he attended with former Presidents Gerald Ford and Jimmy Carter.
Reagan has made very few public appearances since he announced in November 1994 that he had been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, a debilitating neurological disease.
"He's not obviously the outstanding person he was when he was in good health," Ford said. "It's tragic. I can only say that he looks good and we hope for the best."
In addition to the former presidents, their wives, Betty Ford, Rosalynn Carter and Barbara Bush, were in attendance, along with Lady Bird Johnson, widow of the late President Lyndon Johnson.
"We hoped that Mrs. Reagan could have been here on this occasion, but she was reluctant to leave his side under those circumstances," Ford said.

Bush said Reagan's physical appearance is "wonderful," and he "has not lost that wonderful, warm, kind way of dealing with people." He added that he admires Reagan for trying to educate people about the disease.
"It's demoralising. It makes it hard to cope with even a normal situation like this," Bush said.
